neighbours.label: a naming verb introducing an alternative name for something (call it X, known as X, called X by)
fire: Sailors call this wind the mistral.
The Inuit call themselves by a different name.
The plant, commonly known as foxglove, is poisonous.
Fans used to call the stadium the Cauldron.
In Scotland a small lake is called a lochan.
The Romans called the city Lutetia.
This fish is known locally as the sea wolf.
Engineers call this effect thermal runaway.
quiet: Sailors feared this wind in the winter months.
The Inuit live in the far north of Canada.
The plant grows well in shady gardens.
Fans used to sing loudly at the stadium.
In Scotland a small lake can freeze in winter.
The Romans built roads across the region.
This fish is caught locally in spring.
Engineers measured the effect in the lab.
